name: Turkcell Gebze Data Center
notes: Opened 2016 in Gebze (Kocaeli) as Turkey's largest data center; ~35,000 m2, Tier III certified and LEED Gold; 4th module delivered 2021 with 12.6 MW (Serban). Total site MW not publicly disclosed; Turkcell group data-center capacity planned to exceed 64 MW by end-2025 across its facilities.

name: ENKA Data Solutions EDS IST 02 Gebze Data Center
notes: Carrier-neutral colocation facility in Gebze (Beylikbagi, Kocaeli); 18 MW IT load on 30 MW total power, 1,800+ cabinets, 15 kW/cabinet, Uptime Tier III and TS EN 50600, N+2 redundancy, seismic isolation; company also markets 18 MW + 9 MW IT expansion capacity.

name: TUBITAK BILGEM Gebze campus data center infrastructure
notes: National research institute campus in Gebze (Kocaeli) hosting government-grade data-center and certification (Kamu SM certificate authority) infrastructure; no capacity figure disclosed.

name: TURKSAT Konya Data Center project
notes: TURKSAT announced (2017-2019, GM Ensar Gul) a ~50,000 m2 government data center in Konya for public data storage, with tender expected within months; no evidence the Konya facility was completed - TURKSAT's flagship new data center was later anchored at Golbasi, Ankara (groundbreaking 2025). Status uncertain.

name: KOP data-center-region feasibility initiative (Veri Merkezleri Bolgesi Uygunluk Arastirmasi)
developer: KOP Bolge Kalkinma Idaresi (Ministry of Industry and Technology)
notes: 2015 feasibility study by KOP Regional Development Administration to position Konya (low seismic risk, central location) as Turkey's data-center region; no concrete facility built as of publication.

name: Allturko Yer Alti Veri Merkezi (underground data center)
developer: Allturko (Konya-based technology company; chairman Kivanc Kalin)
notes: Anadolu Agency report: ~1 billion TL (~USD 20M) underground data center in Nevsehir, 27 m below ground, 3 floors and 3 corridors; phase 1 = 2 MW, 20 rooms, ~200 cabinets (mostly pre-sold); phase 2 target 5 MW; supported by Ministry of Industry and Technology and Ahiler Development Agency; construction expected to start during 2026, service in ~28 months; promoted as first such facility in Turkey.

name: Kapadokya (Cappadocia) rock-cut storage conversion to data centers
notes: Initiative to convert Nevsehir/Cappadocia's natural rock-cut storage caverns into energy-efficient data centers (natural insulation cuts cooling costs); no concrete investor or completed facility confirmed.

name: MUSKI new data center
developer: MUSKI (Mugla Water and Sewerage Administration / Mugla Metropolitan Municipality)
notes: Mugla utility's newly commissioned data center equipped with redundant power sources and advanced security systems to strengthen municipal services; no MW figure disclosed.
